title: Tinted canvas
oneline: Deeper cool ground, white panels, a hairline ring instead of a drop shadow, and the house indigo as a command bar across the top.
feel: A modern administrative console. Closest to what is live, but the ground is darker so the panels read as paper laid on a desk rather than as faint boxes.

title: Warm document
oneline: Warm paper ground, no shadows anywhere, near-square corners, and mono uppercase panel headings.
feel: A district return rather than a web app. Nothing floats and nothing glows; every division on the screen is a printed rule. Calm on a long afternoon, and it photographs well in a review slide.

title: Flat sheet
oneline: White page, no cards at all. Sections are divided by a rule and by whitespace, under a near-black service bar.
feel: GOV.UK and USWDS take this line: a card is chrome, and chrome costs reading. The figures sit directly on the page, so a weak monitor and a weak connection both render it faithfully. The least decorated of the four and the fastest to read.

title: Operations desk
oneline: Dark by default: a near-black ground, flat panels, and the KPI figures a size up.
feel: Built to be read from across the room, the way Grafana and Datadog are. The console already carries a validated dark palette, so this is the cheapest of the four to ship, and the only one that is also a correct answer at ten at night.

title: High contrast
oneline: Black ink, 2px rules, no shadows, and every size up a step. Built for a projector and for a reader who is not twenty-five.
feel: The console as it has to look in the review room, thrown on a wall by a projector that washes out everything under 7:1. Nothing here is decoration: every rule is structural and every type size went up one step. It is the least pretty of the eight and the only one that survives bad light.

title: Dense console
oneline: The 8pt grid run at 6pt and every type size down a step, so appreciably more of the district fits on one screen.
feel: For the reader who wants the whole morning in one view and will not scroll for it. It buys about a fifth of the page height back. What it costs is reading comfort and, on a phone, touch targets, which is why the phone keeps the full sizes.

title: Elevated
oneline: Material 3 proper: a tonal indigo ground, 20px panels on real elevation, and fully rounded controls.
feel: The most conventionally modern of the eight, and the one a visitor would call finished. Elevation does the grouping that rules do elsewhere. The cost is that soft shadows are the first thing a cheap monitor renders as mud, which is the ground the console already walked away from once.

title: Editorial
oneline: Serif headings, hairline rules, one accent and a great deal of air. The register as a published document.
feel: The only one of the eight that does not look like software. Headings are set in Georgia, which is on every machine already and is not a webfont, so the app still opens with no signal. It reads slowly and deliberately, which suits a screen that issues notices and does not suit one somebody scans at eight in the morning.
